statement: Honda chassis families in 2020-2025: CRF450R 2020 (old frame), CRF450R 2021-2024 (frame 50010-MKE-AF0 in 2021-2022, revised 50010-MKE-AS0 in 2023-2024), CRF250R 2020-2021 (old frame), CRF250R 2022-2024 (the CRF450R-style frame 50010-MKE-AF0), and the 2025 CRF250R and CRF450R sharing a new frame 50010-K95-AG0. Parts listed with the same number cross freely inside a family; across families check each part.
notes: Honda says the 2025 frame has about 70% new parts with relocated subframe mounts, new triple clamps, fork tubes, front axle and one-piece linkage. Part numbers are from the Australian Honda parts catalogue (same CRF-R chassis parts as other markets in the years compared, but confirm against a US fiche if your bike is a US model). 2026-2027 were not in the catalogue checked.

statement: The front wheel crosses every year: CRF250R and CRF450R share front wheel 44650-MKE-AF0 (450 from 2021, 250 from 2022 through 2025; 2020 bikes list 44650-MKE-A70), and all years use the same front hub 44635-MKE-A60, the same front wheel collars (44311-MKE-A60, 44312-KRN-A30) and the same distance collar. Catch: the 2025 bikes use a new front axle (44301-K95-AG0, 2020-2024 is 44301-MEN-000), new fork tubes and a new front disc and caliper, so a wheel moved between 2025 and earlier bikes must use the axle and disc of the bike it goes on.
notes: Part numbers are from the Australian Honda parts catalogue (same CRF-R chassis parts as other markets in the years compared, but confirm against a US fiche if your bike is a US model). 2026-2027 were not in the catalogue checked.

statement: Rear wheels swap across 2020-2025 CRF250R and CRF450R: the rear axle (42301-KRN-A30), axle collars and final-drive sprocket mount are the same every year, and both models use rear hub 42635-MKE-AF0 from 2022 (450 from 2021). Catch: the CRF450R rear wheel (42650-MKE-AF0) has a 19x2.15 rim and the CRF250R wheel (42650-K95-AA0) a 19x1.85 rim, so a 250 wheel on a 450 runs a narrower rim (and the reverse). The 2025 bikes keep the same rear wheel but use a new rear disc (43351-K95-AG1; 2020-2024 is 43351-KRN-A90). The rear caliper (43150-MKE-A01) is the same 2020-2025.

statement: Rear sprockets bolt onto every 2020-2025 CRF250R and CRF450R: the drive-sprocket part 41201-MKE-A70 and the 48/50/51-tooth driven sprockets (41202-MKE-A00, 41203-MKE-A00, 41204-MKE-A10) are listed across models and years. statement: Complete forks and shocks carry different numbers almost every year because the valving changes (for example CRF450R right fork 51400-MKE-AF2 in 2022, 51400-MKE-AS1 in 2023-2024, 51400-MKE-BD1 in 2025), but inside one chassis family they bolt in: same steering stem and top bridge family, same shock mounts and linkage. Across families they do not: the 2025 bikes have new fork tubes, triple clamps (top bridge 53300-K95-AG0, stem 53219-K95-AG0) and a one-piece linkage (cushion arm 52465-K95-AG0). A 2021-2024 fork or shock in a 2025 frame, or the reverse, is not a listed fit. Expect different valving and springs when swapping across years.
notes: Fit inside a family is inferred from identical clamps, stem, linkage and swingarm part numbers, not from a Honda statement that each fork fits each year. Part numbers are from the Australian Honda parts catalogue (same CRF-R chassis parts as other markets in the years compared, but confirm against a US fiche if your bike is a US model). 2026-2027 were not in the catalogue checked.

topic: generation boundary: what changed for 2023 (chassis parts)
statement: KTM's 2023 SX and SX-F motocross bikes are a new generation: new hydroformed frame, new die-cast swingarm, new aluminium-polyamide subframe, new bodywork and a new WP XACT shock. Treat 2020-2022 and 2023-on as two separate families for frame, swingarm, subframe, plastics, seat, airbox, rear wheel, triple clamps and exhaust; parts do not cross that line unless KTM lists them for both. Catch: the 2022 450 SX-F and 250 SX-F Factory Edition (released early 2022) already used the 2023-generation chassis, so a "2022" Factory Edition takes 2023-on parts, not 2020-2022 parts.
notes: The 2022 Factory Edition press info lists the new hydroformed frame, die-cast swingarm, aluminium-polyamide hybrid subframe, new bodywork and new XACT fork and shock; the 2023 range carried that chassis. The 2023 two-strokes (125/250/300 SX) moved onto the same new chassis in 2023 (the 250 SX skipped the 2023 US model year). Generation split also visible in every KTM PowerParts fitment list in this file.

source.name: KTM press info, 2022 450 SX-F and 250 SX-F Factory Edition

topic: generation boundary: what changed for 2023 (chassis parts)
statement: Husqvarna's TC and FC moved to a new chassis for 2023 (new hydroformed frame, die-cast swingarm, aluminium-polyamide subframe, new bodywork, new WP XACT fork and shock). Treat 2020-2022 and 2023-on as two families for frame, swingarm, subframe, plastics, seat, airbox, rear wheel, triple clamps and exhaust. Catch: the 2022 FC 450 and FC 250 Rockstar Edition already used the 2023-generation chassis, so they take 2023-on parts.

source.name: Husqvarna news, 2022 Rockstar Editions

topic: generation boundary: GasGas changed a year later (2024)
statement: GasGas kept the older chassis through 2023 and moved its MC motocross bikes to the new generation (new frame, die-cast swingarm, new subframe and bodywork) for 2024. So a GasGas 2021-2023 shares old-generation parts with a 2020-2022 KTM or Husqvarna, and a GasGas 2024-on shares new-generation parts with a 2023-on KTM or Husqvarna, where the same part number is listed. Catch: the 2023 MC 450F and MC 250F Factory Edition (released December 2022) previewed the 2024 chassis; a standard 2023 MC-F is the older 2021-2023 chassis. Check which one you have before buying.
notes: A magazine reprints the GasGas spec list (new generation frame, new aluminium subframe, new die-cast swingarm, new bodywork) for the 2023 Factory Edition and calls it a preview of the 2024 production bike. The 2024 boundary for standard bikes matches every GASGAS Technical Accessories fitment list in this file (old-generation parts end at 2023, new-generation parts start at 2024). Tier OEM because the content is the maker spec list and the maker fitment lists; confidence medium because the article is a reprint.

source.name: Cycle News 2023 GasGas Factory Edition first look

topic: 2025 frame and linkage update inside the 2023-on generation
statement: For 2025 KTM reworked the SX-F frame (material removed around the head tube, engine mounts and shock tower, same geometry), fitted shorter, slimmer linkage arms with smaller bolts and new seals, and new engine mounts. Bodywork, wheels, triple clamps and most bolt-on parts still interchange 2023-2027, but linkage arms, linkage bolts and seals and engine mounts from a 2023-2024 bike are not the same parts as 2025-on. Aftermarket linkages are sold in separate 2023-2024 and 2025-on versions.

vals.unchanged_2023_2027: frame geometry, wheels, triple clamps, most bodywork
vals.changed_2025: frame tubes/cut-outs, linkage arms and bolts (smaller), linkage seals, engine mounts, tank shrouds

notes: Bolt sizes reported by a magazine: 17 to 15 mm and 17 to 14 mm. A suspension tuner sells its linkage in a "2024.5 and up" version made to fit the 2025 frames, which matches the change (TUNER tier, one source).

source.name: KTM model page, 2025 KTM 450 SX-F

topic: 2025 frame and linkage update inside the 2023-on generation
statement: For 2025 the KTM SX two-strokes got a revised chromoly frame (wall thickness, front triangle and shock mount), new engine mounts, new linkage and new tank shrouds. Wheels, triple clamps, seat and most bolt-on parts still interchange 2023-2027, but linkage parts, engine mounts and tank shrouds from a 2023-2024 bike are not the same as 2025-on.

vals.changed_2025: frame, engine mounts, linkage, tank shrouds, brake pedal

notes: The 2025 change list is from a 2025 first-look article (ultimatemotorcycling.com, 2024-04); the KTM model page confirms the 2025 frame and linkage carried into 2026.

topic: 2025 frame and linkage update inside the 2023-on generation
statement: Husqvarna's 2025 TC and FC got the same frame material removal around the shock mount, new engine mounts, new linkage seals and smaller linkage bolts, a 5 mm higher and wider seat, new side panels and Brembo brakes and clutch (2023-2024 used Braktec). So 2023-2024 and 2025-on Husqvarnas share wheels and triple clamps, but not seat, side panels, linkage hardware or brake and clutch hydraulics.

vals.changed_2025: frame, engine mounts, linkage seals and bolts, seat (+5 mm), side panels, brakes and clutch to Brembo

notes: Husqvarna Technical Accessories list separate seats (A36007040000C1A for 2023-2024, A36007040100C1A for 2025-2026) and separate air-filter-box covers for 2025-on, which agrees.

statement: One front wheel fits every KTM SX/SX-F and Husqvarna TC/FC from 2020 to 2027: KTM lists its Factory front wheel 1.6x21 (A46009901044C1) for all 2020-2027 SX and SX-F models, and Husqvarna lists the same number for all its 2020-2027 TC and FC. The front axle and axle puller are also listed across all years. So a front wheel from any 2020-2027 KTM or Husqvarna motocross bike bolts into any other with its own spacers.

The 2023-on Factory Racing front wheel A46009901544C1A is only listed 2023-on; that does not stop the base wheel crossing years. Disc and spacers: keep the disc that matches your caliper (see brake records). Front brake disc A46009960000 is also listed for every year.

topic: rear wheel: 2020-2022 and 2023-on do not swap
statement: Rear wheels split at the 2023 chassis change. KTM lists its Factory rear wheel 2.15x18/19 as 7901090214430 / 7901090114430 for 2020-2022 and as A4901090104404 / A4601090104404 for 2023-2027, and the 2023-on wheel uses its own spacer set (A46010916044) and its own rear caliper support (A46013975044, 2020-2022 is 77713975044). So a 2020-2022 rear wheel is not listed for a 2023-on bike or the other way round. Within 2020-2022, and within 2023-2027, rear wheels swap freely between SX, SX-F, TC and FC. Catch: the 2022 450 SX-F and 250 SX-F Factory Edition (released early 2022) already used the 2023-generation chassis, so a "2022" Factory Edition takes 2023-on parts, not 2020-2022 parts.
notes: 2020-2022 wheel: https://www.ktm.com/en-us/parts---wear/powerparts/products.html?c1=1001509725&c2=1001509728&product=1002059116. Husqvarna lists the same split (7901090214430 for 2020-2022, A4901090104468 for 2023-on). KTM gives no reason; the separate spacer set and caliper support show the axle-side hardware changed with the new swingarm. Do not assume a 2022 wheel goes into a 2023 bike with spacers.

topic: rear wheel: GasGas 2021-2023 and 2024-on do not swap
statement: GasGas lists the old-generation Factory rear wheel (7901090214430 18 in / 7901090114430 19 in) for 2021-2023 MC models and the new-generation wheel (A49010901144FA / A46010901044FA) with spacer set A46010916044 for 2024-2027. A 2021-2023 GasGas rear wheel swaps with a 2020-2022 KTM or Husqvarna rear wheel; a 2024-on GasGas rear wheel swaps with a 2023-on KTM or Husqvarna one. Catch: the 2023 MC 450F and MC 250F Factory Edition (released December 2022) previewed the 2024 chassis; a standard 2023 MC-F is the older 2021-2023 chassis. Check which one you have before buying.

source.name: GASGAS Technical Accessories browser (gasgas.com US), accessory fitment by model year

topic: triple clamps and handlebar mounts: split at 2023
statement: Triple clamps and bar mounts do not cross the 2023 change. KTM lists Factory Racing triple clamps 79101999021C1A and stock-type clamps 7810199902204 for 2020-2022, and A46001999021C1A / A4900199902204 for 2023-2027; handlebar mounts are 790019390xx (2020-2022) versus A480010390xx (2023-2027). Inside each range the same clamp fits every SX and SX-F (two- and four-stroke) and the same Factory Racing clamp is listed for Husqvarna TC/FC. The 2023-on Factory Racing clamp offers 20-22 mm adjustable offset. Catch: the 2022 450 SX-F and 250 SX-F Factory Edition (released early 2022) already used the 2023-generation chassis, so a "2022" Factory Edition takes 2023-on parts, not 2020-2022 parts.
notes: 2020-2022 clamp listing: https://www.ktm.com/en-us/parts---wear/powerparts/products.html?c1=1001509634&c2=1002622597&product=1001633447. Husqvarna lists 79101999021C1A for 2020-2022 TC/FC and A46001999021C1A for 2023-on. Whole fork legs: the clamp diameter and fork family differ between generations (new XACT fork for 2023), so swap forks with their own clamps.

source.name: KTM PowerParts browser (ktm.com US), accessory fitment by model year

topic: triple clamps and handlebar mounts: GasGas split at 2024
statement: GasGas lists Factory Racing triple clamp 79701999021FAA (or KTM's 79101999021C1A family) for 2021-2023 MC models and A46001999021FAA / A46001999021C1A for 2024-2027; handlebar mount kits are 797019391xx (2021-2023) and A480010390xx (2024-2027). The 2024-on clamp is the same number KTM and Husqvarna list for 2023-on bikes, so a KTM or Husqvarna 2023-on Factory Racing clamp fits a 2024-on GasGas. Stock GasGas clamps are forged rather than CNC-machined. Catch: the 2023 MC 450F and MC 250F Factory Edition (released December 2022) previewed the 2024 chassis; a standard 2023 MC-F is the older 2021-2023 chassis. Check which one you have before buying.

source.name: GASGAS Technical Accessories browser (gasgas.com US), accessory fitment by model year

statement: KTM plastics do not cross the 2023 change: kits 00010000310/311/319/320 are listed for 2020-2022 and the 2023-on kits for 2023-2027 only; front fender 79008010000 (2020-2022) versus A46008010000 (2023-2027), front number plate 79108007100 versus A46008007000, airbox side panel 79106903000 versus A46006903000. Inside 2023-2027 the fender, number plate and side panels carry over, and kit 00010000430K/431K is listed for every 2023-2027 model, but some kits are listed only 2023-2024 (00010000383K) or only 2025-2027 (00010000429K) because KTM changed the tank shrouds for 2025. So a 2023-2024 shroud set is not a 2025-on part.
notes: 2025-2027 kit: https://www.ktm.com/en-us/parts---wear/powerparts/products.html?c1=1001509774&c2=1001509775&product=1003783919. 2025 new shrouds are in KTM's 2025 change list. Plastics are brand-specific: Husqvarna and GasGas bodywork has its own numbers and shape (see their records).

source.name: KTM PowerParts browser (ktm.com US), accessory fitment by model year

statement: Husqvarna plastics kits are listed in three groups: 00010000313/322 for 2020-2022, 00010000373K-379K for 2023-2024, and 00010000433K-435K for 2025-2027 (2025 brought new side panels). Front fender A36008010000 and front number plate A36008007000 carry across 2023-2027; 2020-2022 use 25008010000 and 25108007000. Husqvarna bodywork does not fit a KTM or GasGas: the subframe-side panels and airbox cover differ. Catch: the 2022 FC 450 and FC 250 Rockstar Edition already used the 2023-generation chassis, so they take 2023-on parts.

source.name: Husqvarna Technical Accessories browser (husqvarna-motorcycles.com US), accessory fitment by model year

topic: plastics and bodywork: GasGas split at 2024
statement: GasGas plastics kits are 00010000348/349 for 2021-2023 and 00010000396K/398K/400K for 2024-2027; front fender A54008010000 (2021-2023) versus A59008010000 (2024-2027); airbox panel A54006003000 versus A59006004000. GasGas bodywork is its own shape and does not take KTM or Husqvarna plastics, even on the shared frame. Catch: the 2023 MC 450F and MC 250F Factory Edition (released December 2022) previewed the 2024 chassis; a standard 2023 MC-F is the older 2021-2023 chassis. Check which one you have before buying.

source.name: GASGAS Technical Accessories browser (gasgas.com US), accessory fitment by model year

statement: KTM seats split at 2023: Factory Racing seat 79107040100 / 79707240000 for 2020-2022 and A46007040000C1A for 2023-2027, same seat for two- and four-strokes. A 2023-on seat does not fit a 2020-2022 subframe and the reverse. Inside 2023-2027 the same seat is listed for every year.
notes: Husqvarna and GasGas seats are different parts (own subframe-side shape and seat mount).

source.name: KTM PowerParts browser (ktm.com US), accessory fitment by model year

statement: Husqvarna seats come in three groups: 25107240000 for 2020-2022, A36007040000C1A for 2023-2024 (and the 2022 FC Rockstar Edition), and A36007040100C1A for 2025-on, when the seat became 5 mm higher and wider. A 2023-2024 seat is not listed for a 2025-on bike.
notes: The 2025-on Factory Racing seat number comes from an official dealer listing (lings.com) rather than the Husqvarna browser.

source.name: Husqvarna Technical Accessories browser (husqvarna-motorcycles.com US), accessory fitment by model year

statement: GasGas seats split at 2024: Factory Racing seat A54007040000FBA for 2021-2023 and A54107940000FBA (Factory seat A59007040000FBA) for 2024-2027. GasGas seats do not take KTM or Husqvarna seats. Catch: the 2023 MC 450F and MC 250F Factory Edition (released December 2022) previewed the 2024 chassis; a standard 2023 MC-F is the older 2021-2023 chassis. Check which one you have before buying.

source.name: GASGAS Technical Accessories browser (gasgas.com US), accessory fitment by model year

topic: rear sprocket and chain: same across all years and models
statement: Rear sprockets and chains interchange across every KTM SX/SX-F, Husqvarna TC/FC and GasGas MC from 2020 to 2027, two- and four-stroke: KTM lists rear sprockets 5821095104x (and Renthal A4601095104x, Supersprox 81310951045xx) for all of them, and the same chains (520, 118 links: 78910065118, 50310165118, 78010267118 X-ring) for every year. Front sprockets 7973392901x are listed for all KTM SX and SX-F 2020-2027. Only tooth count changes stock gearing.
notes: Chain listing: https://www.ktm.com/en-us/parts---wear/powerparts/products.html?c1=1001509658&c2=1001509661&product=1002059130. Husqvarna and GASGAS browsers list the same rear sprocket and chain numbers for 2020-2027 / 2021-2027. GasGas lists its own front sprocket numbers (A540339290xx) for MC models.

source.name: KTM PowerParts browser (ktm.com US), accessory fitment by model year

statement: The front brake disc carries over every year: KTM lists front disc A46009960000 (and Wave disc 25010960000) for all 2020-2027 SX and SX-F, and Husqvarna lists the same numbers. KTM brake lever 7871399204404 and clutch lever 7800293120004 are listed for every 2020-2027 KTM. The rear caliper support changed in 2023 (77713975044 for 2020-2022, A46013975044 for 2023-on). Catch on Husqvarna: 2023-2024 TC/FC used Braktec brake and clutch hydraulics and 2025-on use Brembo, so levers, master cylinders and calipers are not the same parts across those years even though the disc is.
notes: Oversize 270 mm front disc kits need their own caliper support (78913914100). Husqvarna brake brands per year come from the 2025 Husqvarna change list.

source.name: KTM PowerParts browser (ktm.com US), accessory fitment by model year

statement: The front disc A46009960000 is listed for every GasGas MC 2021-2027 (same as KTM), but GasGas uses Braktec brakes and clutch hydraulics, not Brembo, and lists its own levers (78713992044FAA / 78002931200FAA for 2021-2023, A54013901044FAA / A54002931044FAA for 2023-on) and its own Wave disc A59009960000 for 2024-on. So KTM levers, master cylinders and calipers are not listed for GasGas. Note: 2022-2025 GasGas MC and EX front Braktec calipers were recalled in Australia for cracking.

source.name: GASGAS Technical Accessories browser (gasgas.com US), accessory fitment by model year

topic: four-stroke exhaust (header and silencer) fit by generation and engine
statement: Four-stroke exhausts are generation- and engine-specific. Akrapovic slip-on 79505979000 fits the 2020-2022 KTM 250 and 450 SX-F (and 2020-2022 FC 250/450, 2021-2023 MC 250F/450F); for the new generation it is A46005979000 for the 250 SX-F and A48005979000 for the 350 and 450 SX-F (2023-2027, also FC and 2024-on MC). Full systems and FMF headers are listed per engine (for example FMF Megabomb header 79505907501 for the 2020-2022 450, A46005907501 for the 2023-on 250). A 2020-2022 pipe does not fit a 2023-on bike. Catch for 2026-on: KTM lists a new slip-on A47005979000 for 2026-2027 SX-F, and US 2027 standard SX-F (and 2026 Factory Editions) use a different airbox and filter for sound rules; to fit the race exhaust KTM says to change the airbox and filter back to 2025 parts and load the matching map, after which the bike no longer meets the sound limit.
notes: 2026-27 slip-on: https://www.ktm.com/en-us/parts---wear/powerparts/products.html?c1=1001509590&c2=1001509592&product=1004502429. Airbox note comes from KTM PowerParts fitting notes (see p5_ktm_group_mx.json record on US MY27 intake). The Husqvarna FC 250 is listed for new-generation parts from 2022 because of the Rockstar Edition.

source.name: KTM PowerParts browser (ktm.com US), accessory fitment by model year

topic: two-stroke pipe and silencer fit by generation
statement: Two-stroke pipes split at 2023: FMF Factory Fatty 50505907001 (125) and 55505907001 (250) fit 2020-2022 KTM SX and Husqvarna TC; for 2023-on it is A42005907001 (125 SX/TC 125) and A44005907001 (250 SX 2024-on, 300 SX, TC 250). Akrapovic silencers follow the same split (50505979000 / 55505979000 old, A42005979000 / A44005979000 new), and KTM lists a separate silencer A45005979000 for 2027 250/300 SX and TC 250. A 2020-2022 pipe does not fit a 2023-on frame.

source.name: KTM PowerParts browser (ktm.com US), accessory fitment by model year

topic: airbox and air filter: split at 2023
statement: Airbox parts and filters do not cross the 2023 change: KTM lists air filter 79006015000 for 2016-2022, airbox front part 79106001010 and filter wash cover 7900699810004 for 2020-2022, and airbox front part A46006001010 and wash cover A46006998000 for 2023-2027 (same wash cover on 2023-on Husqvarna and 2024-on GasGas). Catch: 2026 Factory Editions and US 2027 standard SX-F use a different airbox and filter to meet sound rules.

source.name: KTM PowerParts browser (ktm.com US), accessory fitment by model year

statement: On the 2020-2022 generation, Pivot Pegz 79703940044 and the footpeg slider kit fit every KTM SX/SX-F and Husqvarna TC/FC, and the Factory Racing radiator kit 79535910044 fits both the 450 SX-F and FC 450. Neither part is listed for the 2023-on chassis, so do not assume they carry over.
notes: GasGas lists the same Pivot Pegz and 450 radiator kit for its 2021-2023 MC models.

source.name: KTM PowerParts browser (ktm.com US), accessory fitment by model year

topic: fork and shock: generation-specific, swap as complete units with clamps
statement: The 2023 generation brought a new WP XACT fork and a new, shorter XACT shock with new linkage. KTM lists fork adjuster parts (rebound adjuster A46004925033, adjuster kit 00010000413) only for 2023-2027. So a 2020-2022 shock is not a direct fit in a 2023-on frame (the shock and linkage changed together), and forks should be swapped together with their own triple clamps. 2025-on linkage hardware differs again from 2023-2024.
notes: Shock length change (15 mm shorter on the 2023 450 SX-F) is from a magazine; KTM press info for the 2022 Factory Edition says "new WP XACT rear shock design". Whole fork and shock part numbers per year are compared in the fiche-based records below when available.

source.name: KTM PowerParts browser (ktm.com US), accessory fitment by model year

topic: OEM part numbers: wheels, hubs and axles
statement: KTM's spare-parts catalogue confirms the split: front wheel complete 7900900144430 and front hub 77709010144 are listed on every 125 SX, 250 SX, 300 SX, 250 SX-F and 450 SX-F from 2020 to 2026, so front wheels swap across all of them. The rear wheel is 7901000134430 on 2020-2022 bikes and A4601000104430 on 2023-on bikes, with a new rear hub (A36010010044) and new rear axle (A46010185044) from 2023, unchanged through 2026. So a 2020-2022 rear wheel and a 2023-on rear wheel are different parts with different hubs and axles: do not swap them.
notes: Compared on the 2020-2025 125 SX, 250 SX, 2023-2024 300 SX and 2020-2024 250/450 SX-F pages (US 4T, EU and US 2T) and all 2025-2026 models. 2027 was not in the catalogue. Agrees with the PowerParts wheel listings above.

source.name: Sun City Motorcycles OEM parts fiche (KTM spare-parts catalogue, US and EU models, part numbers by model year)

topic: OEM part numbers: frames, top clamp, linkage, radiators and air filter
statement: The spare-parts catalogue shows the frame split at 2023 (450 SX-F 7950300100033 / 79503001000EB in 2020-2022, A46003001000C1 in 2023-2024; 125 SX 50503001000 in 2020-2022, A42003001000C1 in 2023-2024 and A42003001200C1 in 2025). The 2023-on top triple clamp A46001134022C1 (22 mm offset) is the same part on two- and four-strokes. The linkage triangle lever is 7910408004401 (2021-2022), A46004080044 with an M16 pin (2023-2024) and A46004080244 with an M14 pin (2025-2026), confirming the 2025 linkage change; the 2025 frames are new numbers (A46003001200C1 SX-F, A44003001200C1 250/300 SX) and carry into 2026. The 2023-on radiators (A46035007000 left, A46035008000 right) are listed on both the 125 SX and 450 SX-F; for 2026 the right radiator became A46035008100 (threaded cap). Air filter A46006015000 fits every 2023-2026 SX and SX-F, except the 2026 EU-market 125 SX, which lists filter A48006015000 and its own filter support (sound-rule airbox).
notes: The 250 SX-F 2020-2022 frame is 7910300120033 / 79103001200EB (shared with the 350 SX-F family), the 450 its own 795 frame, so old-generation frames are engine-specific.

source.name: Sun City Motorcycles OEM parts fiche (KTM spare-parts catalogue, US and EU models, part numbers by model year)

topic: front wheel, rear hub, axles and chain: shared across all TF models
statement: Every TF motocross bike uses the same front wheel (T2009269, 1.6x21) with the same hub, spindle, spacer and bearings, and the same rear hub (T2015093), rear spindle (T2011135), rear spacers, chain adjuster blocks, 48T rear sprocket (T2015061) and 520 x 114-link chain (T2015057). So a front wheel swaps between any TF 250-X and TF 450. Catch on the rear wheel: the TF 250-X rear wheel (T2015094) has a 1.85x19 rim and the TF 450 (T2015046) a 2.15x19 rim; the hub and axle are the same, so it bolts in, but the rim width (and tire size) differs.
notes: Catalogues compared: TF 250-X 2024-2025 (catalogue CC7868), TF 250-X 2026 (CF3825), TF 450-RC Edition (2025) and TF 450-X (2026). TF 450-X rear wheel page: https://www.triumphpartstore.com/us/catalog/assembly/23713?catalogue=T.

source.name: Triumph Waukesha OEM parts catalogue, part numbers per assembly

topic: frame, swingarm and footpegs: shared; subframe and shock differ 250 vs 450
statement: All TF models list the same main frame (T2078475), the same swingarm (T2051612) and pivot spindle, and the same footpegs (T2083238/T2083239) and clevises. The rear subframe differs: T2074959 on the TF 250-X (all years) and T2075413 on the TF 450-RC Edition and TF 450-X. The shock is model-specific (TF 250-X T2051711, TF 450-RC T2053015, TF 450-X T2054044). Engine head-steady brackets also differ by model. So a 450 subframe is not listed for a 250 and the reverse.
notes: Catalogues compared: TF 250-X 2024-2025 (catalogue CC7868), TF 250-X 2026 (CF3825), TF 450-RC Edition (2025) and TF 450-X (2026). TF 450-X frame page: https://www.triumphpartstore.com/us/catalog/assembly/23715?catalogue=T.

source.name: Triumph Waukesha OEM parts catalogue, part numbers per assembly

topic: forks and triple clamps: 250 and 450 units differ
statement: The TF 250-X (2024-2026) uses forks T2043161/T2043162 with lower yoke T2044587 and upper yoke T2044585; the TF 450-RC Edition and TF 450-X use forks T2046481/T2046482 with lower yoke T2046421 and upper yoke T2046411 (different cartridge and base valve). Fork seals, bleed screws and the spring seat are shared, and the 4.8 and 4.9 N/mm spring kits are listed for both. Swap forks as complete sets with their own yokes; a 450 fork in a 250 needs the 450 yokes too, and Triumph lists no such conversion.

vals.shared: fork seal kit T2045341, spring kits K4.8/K4.9

notes: Catalogues compared: TF 250-X 2024-2025 (catalogue CC7868), TF 250-X 2026 (CF3825), TF 450-RC Edition (2025) and TF 450-X (2026). Clamp dimensions are not published; "swap with yokes" is the safe reading of different yoke part numbers. The 2027 TF 250-X adds Neken clamps (not in this catalogue). TF 450-X fork page: https://www.triumphpartstore.com/us/catalog/assembly/23699?catalogue=T.

source.name: Triumph Waukesha OEM parts catalogue, part numbers per assembly

topic: bodywork and seat: 2026 changed side panels and airbox covers
statement: Front mudguard T2313252 fits every TF. The seat (T2310994) is the same on the TF 250-X 2024-2026 and TF 450-X (the RC Edition has its own gripper seat). The 2026 TF 250-X and the TF 450-X share new tank side covers (T2313590/T2313591), airbox covers (T2313663/T2313667) and rear mudguard (T2313790); the 2024-2025 TF 250-X uses older covers (T2310630/T2310631 or T2313890/T2313891) and the RC Edition its own. So 2024-2025 TF 250-X side panels are not the 2026 parts. Triumph's MX plastics kit A9700932 is listed for the TF 250-X 2024-2026 and TF 450.
notes: Catalogues compared: TF 250-X 2024-2025 (catalogue CC7868), TF 250-X 2026 (CF3825), TF 450-RC Edition (2025) and TF 450-X (2026). Plastics kit fitment from the Triumph accessory catalogue (dealer-triumph-genuine.json, assembly 23283). Two cover numbers on the 2024-2025 catalogue are likely a supersession.

source.name: Triumph Waukesha OEM parts catalogue, part numbers per assembly

statement: The TF 250-X header pipe (T2205896) is the same 2024-2026, but the silencer changed for 2026 (T2204970 on 2024-2025, T2209937 on 2026) along with the airbox (front and rear) for sound rules. The TF 450 has its own header (T2205916) and silencer (T2208154). The foam air filter (T2205329) fits every TF. Akrapovic systems from Triumph are listed separately for the 2024-2025 TF 250-X (A9601343) and the 2026 TF 250-X (A9601349/A9601360), and for the TF 450 (A9601344/A9601361).
notes: Catalogues compared: TF 250-X 2024-2025 (catalogue CC7868), TF 250-X 2026 (CF3825), TF 450-RC Edition (2025) and TF 450-X (2026). 2024-2025 exhaust page: https://www.triumphpartstore.com/us/catalog/assembly/23213?catalogue=T.

statement: The 2026 TF 250-X radiators (T2105040/T2105041) are the same parts as the TF 450-RC and TF 450-X; the 2024-2025 TF 250-X uses T2105030/T2105031. Radiator guards (T2101531/T2101532) fit every TF.
notes: Catalogues compared: TF 250-X 2024-2025 (catalogue CC7868), TF 250-X 2026 (CF3825), TF 450-RC Edition (2025) and TF 450-X (2026).

topic: four-stroke chassis families: YZ250F follows the YZ450F a year later
statement: Yamaha four-stroke chassis families (frame part numbers): YZ450F 2020-2022 (B2W frame), YZ450F 2023-2025 (BHR), YZ450F 2026 (D03). The YZ250F runs one year behind on the same frames: 2021-2023 on the B2W frame, 2024-2026 on the BHR frame (Yamaha: "frame based on the 2023 YZ450F"), and 2027 on the D03 frame (Yamaha: YZ450F frame, suspension and bodywork). The 2020 YZ250F is its own (BR9 frame). So inside a family most chassis parts, bodywork and radiators swap between a YZ250F and a YZ450F, and a YZ250F of year N often takes YZ450F parts of year N-1.
notes: Front frame part numbers: B2W-21101-00/-01, BHR-21101-01, D03-21101-00. Part numbers from the Australian Yamaha catalogue; YZ chassis parts are the same in other markets in the years compared, but confirm on a US fiche for a US bike.

source.name: City West Yamaha OEM parts fiche (Yamaha Australia parts catalogue, part numbers by model year)

topic: front wheel: one hub and axle for every YZ250F and YZ450F 2021-2027
statement: Every 2020-2027 YZ250F and YZ450F lists the same front hub (1SL-25111-00), and from 2021 (2020 for the 450) the same front axle (B2W-25181-00), front disc (B2W-2581T-00) and front caliper (B2W-2580T-00). The complete front wheel B2W-25102-00 covers the 2021-2022 YZ450F and 2022 YZ250F, and BSB-25102-00 the 2023-2026 YZ450F and 2023-2026 YZ250F. So a front wheel swaps between any of these bikes. Catch: the 2027 YZ250F lists a new front wheel assembly and front disc (D05) though the hub and axle are unchanged; and the 2020 YZ250F used an older axle (1SL-25181-00).
notes: Part numbers from the Australian Yamaha catalogue; YZ chassis parts are the same in other markets in the years compared, but confirm on a US fiche for a US bike.

source.name: City West Yamaha OEM parts fiche (Yamaha Australia parts catalogue, part numbers by model year)

topic: rear wheel: hub shared from 2022, axle changes with the frame
statement: The YZ250F and YZ450F share rear hub B2W-25311-00 from 2022 through 2027 (2020-2021 is 17D-25311-00), the rear disc B2W-2582W-00 (2021-2026) and the rear caliper B2W-2580W-00. The YZ450F rear wheel B2W-25302-30 is listed for 2022-2025, crossing the 2023 frame change. Catch: the rear axle changed with the new frame (17D-25381-00 up to the 2022 YZ450F and 2023 YZ250F; BHR-25381-00 after), so use the axle and spacers of the bike the wheel goes on; and 2020-2021 rear wheels have the older hub. YZ250F and YZ450F rear wheels carry different assembly numbers (rim and spoke differences), so check rim width. The 2027 YZ450F has a smaller 220 mm rear disc and new caliper, so its rear brake parts do not match earlier years.
notes: 2027 YZ450F rear brake change from Yamaha Australia 2027 spec sheet (yamaha-motor.com.au); the 2027 YZ450F was not yet in the parts catalogue. Part numbers from the Australian Yamaha catalogue; YZ chassis parts are the same in other markets in the years compared, but confirm on a US fiche for a US bike.

source.name: City West Yamaha OEM parts fiche (Yamaha Australia parts catalogue, part numbers by model year)

statement: Yamaha lists the same driven-sprocket numbers (B2W-25447 to 25452 range, 47-52T) for every YZ125, YZ250, YZ250F and YZ450F from 2022 to 2027; 2020-2021 bikes list the older 17D sprocket numbers. All use a 520 chain. So rear sprockets swap across all YZ motocross models 2022-on; only tooth count changes gearing.
notes: The two-stroke rear hub (5ET-25311-00) is unchanged 2020-2027 while the sprocket number changed in 2022, so the older sprockets very likely bolt on, but that is not stated. Part numbers from the Australian Yamaha catalogue; YZ chassis parts are the same in other markets in the years compared, but confirm on a US fiche for a US bike.

source.name: City West Yamaha OEM parts fiche (Yamaha Australia parts catalogue, part numbers by model year)

statement: The top clamp (handle crown B2W-23435-00) and handlebar (BR9-26111-20) are the same on every YZ450F 2020-2026 and YZ250F 2021-2027. The lower clamp changed with the frame: 33D-23340-20 on the YZ450F 2020-2022 and YZ250F 2020-2023, B7R-23340-00 on the YZ450F 2023-on and YZ250F 2024-on. So a complete clamp set swaps inside a family; the top clamp alone swaps across all years.
notes: Part numbers from the Australian Yamaha catalogue; YZ chassis parts are the same in other markets in the years compared, but confirm on a US fiche for a US bike.

source.name: City West Yamaha OEM parts fiche (Yamaha Australia parts catalogue, part numbers by model year)

topic: fork, shock and linkage swap (whole units)
statement: Complete forks and shocks change number almost every year (valving), for example YZ450F fork B2W-23102-20 (2022), BHR-23102-00 (2023-2024), D02-23102-00 (2025), D03-23102-00 (2026). Inside one frame family they bolt in with the matching lower clamp. The linkage relay arm changed for 2025 on both models (17D-2217A-00 up to 2024, D02-2217A-00 from 2025), and the 2026 YZ450F got a new KYB shock and frame, so 2025-on shocks and linkage are not the same parts as earlier ones.
notes: Fit inside a family is inferred from identical clamps, frames and linkage part numbers, not a Yamaha statement. Part numbers from the Australian Yamaha catalogue; YZ chassis parts are the same in other markets in the years compared, but confirm on a US fiche for a US bike.

topic: plastics, seat, subframe, tank and radiators
statement: Bodywork follows the frame family and is shared by both models inside it: front fender BR9-21511 (YZ450F 2020-2022, YZ250F 2020-2023) then BHR-21510 (YZ450F 2023-2026, YZ250F 2024-2027); rear fender, side covers, subframe and tank are BR9 parts on the older bikes, BHR parts on the YZ450F 2023-2025 and YZ250F 2024-2026, and D03 parts on the 2026 YZ450F and 2027 YZ250F. Radiators BR9-12461 (old) and BHR-12461 (YZ450F 2023-2026, YZ250F 2024-2027) are shared by both models. Seats split more often: BR9-24710 (old), BHR-24710 (2023-2024), D02-24710 (2025), D03-24710 (YZ450F 2026, YZ250F 2026-2027).
notes: Part numbers from the Australian Yamaha catalogue; YZ chassis parts are the same in other markets in the years compared, but confirm on a US fiche for a US bike.

statement: Air filter element and footpegs follow the frame family and are shared by both models: element B2W-14451-01 and footrest B2W-27411-00 (YZ450F 2020-2022, YZ250F 2021-2023), then BHR-14451-01 and BHR-27411-00 (YZ450F 2023-on, YZ250F 2024-on). Exhausts are model-specific: YZ250F silencer B7B-14750 (2020-2026, D05 for 2027), YZ450F silencer B2W-14750 (2020-2022), BHR-14750 (2023-2024), D03-14750 (2026). A 250F silencer is not a 450 part.

topic: two-strokes: YZ125 and YZ250 chassis parts barely change 2020-2027
statement: The YZ125 (frame 1SR-21101-00) and YZ250 (frame 1SS-21101-00) keep their frames, triple clamps (lower 1SR/1SS-23340-10, top 1SS-23435-10), swingarm (1C3-22110-A0, 2021-2027), linkage, front hub (5NY-25111-00) and axle (5XC-25181-G0), rear hub (5ET-25311-00) and axle, footpegs (17D-27411-00) and air filter element (4XM-14451-01, same on both) from 2020 to 2027. Front and rear wheels therefore swap between any YZ125 and YZ250 of these years. Bodywork, seat, tank and subframe changed in 2022 (BCR seat and tank, new side covers and rear fender), so 2020-2021 plastics do not fit 2022-on. Brake discs and rear caliper changed number in 2022 (B2W discs, BCR rear caliper). Forks and radiators changed in 2025 (D68 on the YZ125, D69 on the YZ250). Exhaust pipes, subframes and radiators are model-specific (125 vs 250).
notes: No 2023 YZ250 was in the Australian catalogue. Part numbers from the Australian Yamaha catalogue; YZ chassis parts are the same in other markets in the years compared, but confirm on a US fiche for a US bike.

topic: two-stroke and four-stroke wheels do not swap
statement: YZ125/YZ250 wheels use a different front hub (5NY-25111-00) and axle (5XC-25181-G0), and a different rear hub (5ET-25311-00) and axle, from the YZ250F/YZ450F (1SL / B2W front, B2W / 17D or BHR rear). So a four-stroke wheel is not a listed fit on a two-stroke, or the reverse, even though the front master cylinder (5XC-W2587-00) and handlebar are shared.
notes: Part numbers from the Australian Yamaha catalogue; YZ chassis parts are the same in other markets in the years compared, but confirm on a US fiche for a US bike.

topic: ECU / CDI: different, do not swap
statement: Ignition units are model- and year-specific: the YZ125 CDI is 1SR-85540-03 (2020-2021), B4X-85540-00 (2022-2025), D68-85540-00 (2026-2027); the YZ250 CDI 1P8-85540-02 (2020-2025), 1P8-85540-03 (2026-2027). Four-stroke ECUs are tied to each year's engine and maps, and the 2026 YZ450F and YZ250F ECUs carry a password lock. Do not swap ignition units between models or across these changes.
notes: 2026 ECU lock from Yamaha 2026 model information (see yz450f_engine.json / yamaha_250f_2t.json). Four-stroke ECU numbers were not compared in this pass. Part numbers from the Australian Yamaha catalogue; YZ chassis parts are the same in other markets in the years compared, but confirm on a US fiche for a US bike.
